components.description: LEGO Technic 42109, the App-Controlled Top Gear Rally Car, as its instructions build it: a Control+ hub, an XL motor that drives the rear wheels through a differential and an L motor that steers the front wheels through a rack, in a white body with a roll cage and a rear wing; four wheel mounts, the front pair steered, and a seat on the roof. Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.
components.product: LEGO Technic 42109 App-Controlled Top Gear Rally Car

components.name: LEGO Technic 42109 front wheel, Wheel Rim 20 x 30 (56145) with Tyre 22/30 x 30 ZR (44309)
components.description: LEGO Technic wheel rim 20 x 30 (56145) with a 30 mm wide ZR tyre 22/30 x 30 (44309), 43 mm across; the front wheels of 42109.
components.product: LEGO Technic 42109 App-Controlled Top Gear Rally Car

components.name: LEGO Technic 42109 rear wheel, Wheel Rim 20 x 30 (56145) with Tyre 20/48 x 30 (15413)
components.description: LEGO Technic wheel rim 20 x 30 (56145) with a tyre 20/48 x 30 (15413), 50 mm across; the rear wheels of 42109.
components.product: LEGO Technic 42109 App-Controlled Top Gear Rally Car

components.name: LEGO Technic 42124 Off-Road Buggy, without its wheels
components.description: LEGO Technic 42124, the Off-Road Buggy, as its instructions build it: a Control+ hub and two L motors, one that drives the rear wheels through a differential and one that steers the front wheels, on independent suspension with shock absorbers, under a roll cage; four wheel mounts, the front pair steered, and a seat on the roof. Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.

components.name: LEGO Technic 42124 wheel, Wheel Rim 26 x 43 (56908) with Tyre 28/57 x 43 Off Road (69909)
components.description: LEGO Technic wheel rim 26 x 43 (56908) with an off-road tyre 28/57 x 43 (69909), 75 mm across and 28 mm wide; the four wheels of 42124.

components.name: LEGO Technic 42099 4x4 X-treme Off-Roader, without its wheels
components.description: LEGO Technic 42099, the 4x4 X-treme Off-Roader, as its instructions build it: a Control+ hub, two XL motors that drive the front and the rear axle, each through a differential and planetary hubs, and an L motor that steers the front wheels through a rack, on pendular axles; four wheel mounts, the front pair steered, a seat on the roof, and a seat for each XL motor, whose driveline turns its axle's two hubs through the differential and the planetary hubs, so that the car drives all four wheels as the set does. Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.

components.name: LEGO Technic 42099 wheel, Wheel Rim 34 x 56 (15038) with Tyre 44/58 x 56 R Tractor (23798)
components.description: LEGO Technic wheel rim 34 x 56 (15038) with a tractor tyre 44/58 x 56 R (23798), 107 mm across and 44 mm wide; the four wheels of 42099.

components.name: LEGO Education SPIKE Prime Driving Base, without its wheels
components.description: The Driving Base of LEGO Education's SPIKE Prime set 45678 as its building instructions build it: the SPIKE Prime hub on two medium motors that each drive one wheel, a ball caster at the back, and the large motor at the front for attachments, a 12-tooth gear on its output; two wheel mounts, a seat on the hub, and the top_front seat at the hub's front end where the set's distance sensor goes (lego_45678_distance_sensor). Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.

components.name: LEGO Education SPIKE Prime wheel, Wheel 57 x 14 with a medium azure tyre (39367), with the white tooth (48267) on its axle
components.description: The SPIKE Prime wheel, black with four spokes and an integral medium azure tyre (39367), 56 mm across and 14 mm wide, with the white tooth (48267) the Driving Base puts on its axle.

components.name: LEGO Mindstorms NXT 8527 Tri-bot, without its wheels
components.description: The Tri-bot of LEGO Mindstorms NXT 8527 as its instructions build it: the NXT brick on top, two NXT motors that each drive one wheel and a third for a tool at the front, and a rear support of two belt wheels on an axle; two wheel mounts, a seat on the NXT brick, and the front seat where the set's touch sensor attachment goes (lego_8527_touch_sensor), which carries its ultrasonic sensor (lego_8527_ultrasonic_sensor). Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.

components.name: LEGO Mindstorms NXT 8527 wheel, Wheel Rim 20 x 30 (56145) with Tyre 26/52 x 30 Off Road (55976)
components.description: LEGO Technic wheel rim 20 x 30 (56145) with an off-road tyre 26/52 x 30 (55976), 57 mm across; the Tri-bot's driven wheels.

components.name: LEGO Education EV3 Driving Base, without its wheels
components.description: The Driving Base of LEGO Education's EV3 Core Set 45544 as its building instructions build it: the EV3 brick with its rechargeable battery on two large motors that each drive one wheel, a steel ball caster behind the motors, and two white arms at the front for attachments; two wheel mounts, a seat on the brick, the front_sensor seat where the set's ultrasonic sensor goes (lego_45544_ultrasonic_sensor), and the left_arm seat where its touch sensor goes (lego_45544_touch_sensor). Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.
components.product: LEGO Education Mindstorms EV3 Core Set 45544

components.name: LEGO Education EV3 Driving Base wheel, Wheel 43.2 x 26 (56908) with a Tyre 56 x 28 ZR Street (41897), with the white tooth (41669) on its axle
components.description: The EV3 Core Set's wheel, a light bluish grey rim with six pin holes and a black tyre, 56 mm across and 28 mm wide, with the white tooth (41669) the Driving Base puts on its axle.
components.product: LEGO Education Mindstorms EV3 Core Set 45544

components.name: LEGO Education EV3 Ultrasonic Sensor on the Driving Base's bracket
components.description: The EV3 Ultrasonic Sensor on the bracket LEGO Education's instructions build for it, which goes on the EV3 Driving Base (lego_45544_driving_base_chassis) at its front_sensor seat: low at the front, looking forward. It measures the distance to the nearest object in front of it with 40 kHz sound. The bracket is a grey beam 7 and two black T-beams whose two blue pins go into the 5 x 7 frame's free lower holes.
components.product: LEGO Education Mindstorms EV3 Core Set 45544

components.name: LEGO Education SPIKE Prime Distance Sensor on the Driving Base's beam
components.description: The SPIKE Prime Distance Sensor (LEGO Technic 45604) on the beam LEGO Education's instructions build for it, which goes on the SPIKE Prime Driving Base (lego_45678_driving_base_chassis) at its top_front seat: upright on the hub's front end, looking forward. It measures the distance to the nearest object in front of it with ultrasound. The beam is a medium azure beam 7 whose two end pins go into the hub's top corner holes.

components.name: LEGO Technic Control+ XL Motor
components.description: LEGO Technic Control+ XL Motor, as LDraw draws it (22172.dat). It drives a wheel or an axle it is geared to; at 9 V it turns 330 rpm unloaded and stalls at 22 N cm and 1.1 A, as Philippe Hurbain measured.

components.name: LEGO Technic Control+ L Motor
components.description: LEGO Technic Control+ L Motor, as LDraw draws it (22169.dat). It drives a wheel or an axle it is geared to; at 9 V it turns 315 rpm unloaded and stalls at 26 N cm and 1.4 A, as Philippe Hurbain measured.

components.name: LEGO Mindstorms NXT Interactive Servo Motor
components.description: LEGO Mindstorms NXT Interactive Servo Motor, as LDraw draws it (53787.dat). It drives a wheel or an axle it is geared to; at 9 V it turns 170 rpm unloaded and stalls at 50 N cm and 2.0 A, as Philippe Hurbain measured.

components.name: LEGO Technic Medium Angular Motor (SPIKE Prime)
components.description: LEGO Technic Medium Angular Motor (SPIKE Prime), as LDraw draws it (54696p01.dat). It drives a wheel or an axle it is geared to; at 9 V it turns 228 rpm unloaded and stalls at 13.5 N cm and 0.85 A, as Philippe Hurbain measured.

components.name: LEGO Mindstorms EV3 Large Servo Motor
components.description: LEGO Mindstorms EV3 Large Servo Motor, as LDraw draws it (95658.dat). It drives a wheel or an axle it is geared to; at 9 V it turns 175 rpm unloaded and stalls at 43 N cm and 1.8 A, as Philippe Hurbain measured.
components.product: LEGO Education Mindstorms EV3 Core Set 45544

components.name: LEGO Technic 42129 4x4 Mercedes-Benz Zetros Trial Truck, without its wheels
components.description: LEGO Technic 42129, the 4x4 Mercedes-Benz Zetros Trial Truck, as its instructions build it: a Control+ hub, two L motors that drive all four wheels through a centre differential and a differential on each axle, an L motor that steers the front wheels through a rack, and a medium motor that locks the centre and rear differentials, on suspended axles; four wheel mounts, the front pair steered, a seat on the cab's roof, and a seat for each drive motor, whose driveline turns one axle's two hubs. Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.
components.product: LEGO Technic 42129 4x4 Mercedes-Benz Zetros Trial Truck

components.name: LEGO Technic 42129 wheel, Wheel Rim 26 x 43 (56908) with Tyre 35/55 x 43 R Tractor (69912)
components.description: LEGO Technic wheel rim 26 x 43 (56908) with a tractor tyre 35/55 x 43 R (69912), 81 mm across and 34 mm wide; the four wheels of 42129.
components.product: LEGO Technic 42129 4x4 Mercedes-Benz Zetros Trial Truck

components.name: LEGO Technic 42095 Remote-Controlled Stunt Racer, without its tracks
components.description: LEGO Technic 42095, the Remote-Controlled Stunt Racer, as its instructions build it: a Power Functions battery box and infrared receiver on a body that runs on two tracks, each turned by a Power Functions L motor geared 16:16 to its rear sprocket, and steers by the difference of their speeds; two track mounts at the rear sprockets' hubs, a seat on the body's top, and a seat for each motor, whose driveline turns its track. Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.

components.name: LEGO Technic 42095 track, left: 30 reinforced chain tread links (88323) around a 14-tooth and a 10-tooth sprocket
components.description: The left track of LEGO Technic 42095 as its model builds it: 30 reinforced chain tread links (88323), 38.4 mm wide, around the 14-tooth sprocket the motor turns (42529) and a 10-tooth sprocket 104 mm ahead (57519), its run on the ground between them; the belt travels 168 mm per turn of the driven sprocket.

components.name: LEGO Technic 42095 track, right: 30 reinforced chain tread links (88323) around a 14-tooth and a 10-tooth sprocket
components.description: The right track of LEGO Technic 42095 as its model builds it: 30 reinforced chain tread links (88323), 38.4 mm wide, around the 14-tooth sprocket the motor turns (42529) and a 10-tooth sprocket 104 mm ahead (57519), its run on the ground between them; the belt travels 168 mm per turn of the driven sprocket.

components.name: LEGO Power Functions L-Motor
components.description: LEGO Power Functions L-Motor, as LDraw draws it (99499.dat). It drives a wheel, a track or an axle it is geared to; at 9 V it turns 390 rpm unloaded and stalls at 18 N cm and 1.3 A, as Philippe Hurbain measured.

components.name: LEGO Technic 42065 RC Tracked Racer, without its tracks
components.description: LEGO Technic 42065, the RC Tracked Racer, as its instructions build it: a Power Functions battery box and infrared receiver on a body that runs on two tracks, each turned by a Power Functions M motor on the axle of one of its sprockets, the left track's rear one and the right track's front one, with no gears between; it steers by the difference of their speeds. Two track mounts at the driven sprockets' hubs, a seat on the body's top, and a seat for each motor, whose driveline turns its track one to one. Its installed battery and controller feed the modeled drive motors; unpublished electrical limits remain unknown.

components.name: LEGO Technic 42065 track, left: 37 wide tread links (57518) around two 10-tooth sprockets and six road wheels
components.description: The left track of LEGO Technic 42065 as its model builds it: 37 wide tread links (57518), 38.4 mm wide, around two 10-tooth sprockets (57519) 160 mm apart, both clear of the ground, and six road wheels (4185), its run on the ground under the road wheels; the motor turns its rear sprocket, and the belt travels 120 mm per turn of it.

components.name: LEGO Technic 42065 track, right: 37 wide tread links (57518) around two 10-tooth sprockets and six road wheels
components.description: The right track of LEGO Technic 42065 as its model builds it: 37 wide tread links (57518), 38.4 mm wide, around two 10-tooth sprockets (57519) 160 mm apart, both clear of the ground, and six road wheels (4185), its run on the ground under the road wheels; the motor turns its front sprocket, and the belt travels 120 mm per turn of it.

components.name: LEGO Power Functions M-Motor
components.description: LEGO Power Functions M-Motor, as LDraw draws it (58120.dat). It drives a wheel, a track or an axle it is geared to; at 9 V it turns 405 rpm unloaded and stalls at 11 N cm and 850 mA, as Philippe Hurbain measured.

components.name: LEGO Education EV3 Touch Sensor on the Driving Base's left arm
components.description: The EV3 Touch Sensor on the bracket LEGO Education's instructions build for it, which goes on the EV3 Driving Base (lego_45544_driving_base_chassis) at its left_arm seat: low in front of the left wheel, its red button forward. It tells whether its button is pressed. The bracket is a black liftarm 3 x 0.5 and a black beam 2 on an axle 3 through the rail under the sensor's back; the left white arm's axle 4 goes through the liftarm, the rail and the beam.
components.product: LEGO Education Mindstorms EV3 Core Set 45544

components.name: 120:1 Mini Plastic Gearmotor HP, Offset 3mm D-Shaft Output, Extended Motor Shaft
components.description: Pololu 120:1 Mini Plastic Gearmotor HP with an offset 3 mm D-shaft output and an extended motor shaft, the motor of the Romi chassis kit. At 4.5 V it turns 150 rpm unloaded and stalls at 25 oz in (0.18 N m) and 1.25 A; a clutch in its gearbox slips near that load.

components.name: Motor Driver and Power Distribution Board for Romi Chassis
components.description: Pololu Motor Driver and Power Distribution Board for the Romi chassis: two DRV8838 motor drivers, 1.8 A a channel on a 2.5 V to 10.8 V supply, with the Romi's power switch, reverse protection and a 5 V or 3.3 V regulator. It lies on the Romi's deck and solders to its battery contacts.

components.name: Romi 32U4 Control Board
components.description: Pololu Romi 32U4 Control Board: an ATmega32U4 controller with two DRV8838 motor drivers, 1.8 A a channel on a 2.5 V to 10.8 V supply, the Romi's power switch, a 5 V regulator, an accelerometer and gyro, and connections for encoders and a Raspberry Pi. It lies on the Romi's deck and solders to its battery contacts.

components.name: Rechargeable NiMH AA Battery: 1.2 V, 2200 mAh, six cells for the Romi chassis
components.description: Six of Pololu's rechargeable NiMH AA cells, 1.2 V and 2200 mAh each, as the Romi chassis holds them in its battery compartment: two between the motors and four behind them, 7.2 V in series. The cells are sold one at a time; this part is the six a Romi takes.

components.name: 30:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V with Extended Motor Shaft
components.description: Pololu 30:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor MP 6V with an extended motor shaft, the motor of the Standard Edition 3pi+ robots: a brushed motor 10 x 12 mm in section with a metal gearbox between brass plates and a 3 mm D-shaft output. At 6 V it turns 720 rpm unloaded and stalls at 0.33 kg cm (0.032 N m) and 0.67 A.

components.name: 75:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor LP 6V with Extended Motor Shaft
components.description: Pololu 75:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor LP 6V with an extended motor shaft, the motor of the Turtle Edition 3pi+ robots: a brushed motor 10 x 12 mm in section with a metal gearbox between brass plates and a 3 mm D-shaft output. At 6 V it turns 180 rpm unloaded and stalls at 0.64 kg cm (0.063 N m) and 0.36 A.

components.name: 15:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor HPCB 6V with Extended Motor Shaft
components.description: Pololu 15:1 Micro Metal Gearmotor HPCB 6V with an extended motor shaft, the motor of the Hyper Edition 3pi+ robots: a brushed motor with carbon brushes, 10 x 12 mm in section, with a metal gearbox between brass plates and a 3 mm D-shaft output. At 6 V it turns 2100 rpm unloaded and stalls at 0.25 kg cm (0.025 N m) and 1.5 A.

components.name: 3pi+ 2040 Control Board
components.description: Pololu 3pi+ 2040 Control Board: an RP2040 controller with two DRV8838 motor drivers, 1.8 A a channel, on a 2.7 V to 8.5 V supply that a regulator on it turns into a constant 8 V for the motors; with five line sensors, two bump sensors, an IMU, sensors for the motors' encoders, buttons, RGB LEDs and a buzzer. It screws onto a 3pi+ chassis and solders to its battery contacts. Sold without the OLED display it has a header for.

components.name: 3pi+ 32U4 OLED Control Board
components.description: Pololu 3pi+ 32U4 OLED Control Board: an ATmega32U4 controller with two DRV8838 motor drivers, 1.8 A a channel, on a 2.7 V to 6.5 V supply that a regulator on it turns into a constant 8 V for the motors; with five line sensors, two bump sensors, an IMU, sensors for the motors' encoders, buttons and a buzzer. It screws onto a 3pi+ chassis and solders to its battery contacts. Sold without the OLED display it has a header for.

components.name: 3pi+ 32U4 Control Board
components.description: Pololu 3pi+ 32U4 Control Board, the board of the original 3pi+ 32U4 robot with an LCD: an ATmega32U4 controller with two DRV8838 motor drivers, 1.8 A a channel, on a 2.7 V to 6.5 V supply that a regulator on it turns into a constant 8 V for the motors; with five line sensors, two bump sensors, an IMU, sensors for the motors' encoders, buttons and a buzzer. It screws onto a 3pi+ chassis and solders to its battery contacts. Sold without the 8x2 character LCD it has a header for.

components.name: Rechargeable NiMH AAA Battery: 1.2 V, 900 mAh, four cells for a 3pi+ chassis
components.description: Four of Pololu's rechargeable NiMH AAA cells, 1.2 V and 900 mAh each, as a 3pi+ chassis holds them under its control board: two in front of the motors and two behind them, 4.8 V in series. The cells are sold one at a time; this part is the four a 3pi+ takes.

components.name: Graphical OLED Display: 128x64, 1.3", White Pixels, SPI, Black PCB
components.description: Pololu's graphical OLED display, 128 x 64 pixels on a black board, the display of the 3pi+ 2040 and 3pi+ 32U4 OLED robots. It plugs into a header on the control board and stands on two standoffs over it. It shows nothing in simulation.

components.name: 8×2 Character LCD - Black Bezel (Parallel Interface)
components.description: Pololu's 8 x 2 character LCD with a black bezel, the display of the first 3pi+ 32U4 robots. It plugs into a header on the control board and lies over it. It shows nothing in simulation.

components.name: 520 encoder gearmotor, 90:1, 12 V
components.description: Hiwonder JGB37-520R90-12 brushed gearmotor with a Hall encoder: a 37 mm gearbox, 90:1, and a 6 mm D-shaft set 7 mm off the gearbox's centre. At 12 V it turns 110 rpm unloaded and stalls at 15 kg cm (1.47 N m) and 3.2 A. It is the drive motor of Hiwonder's Ackermann chassis, large metal chassis, ROSOrin, JetAuto, JetAcker and JetRover kits, and is sold alone.

components.name: Hiwonder robot battery pack, 11.1 V 6000 mAh
components.description: The battery pack of Hiwonder's ROSOrin, JetAuto, JetAcker and JetRover kits: 11.1 V, 6000 mAh, 86 x 60 x 21 mm, wrapped in black with a white label, an SM discharge plug and a DC charging socket. It comes with those kits and is not sold alone.

components.name: L-type 520 encoder gearmotor, 12 V, 40:1
components.description: Yahboom L-type 520 encoder gearmotor: a 12 V brushed motor beside a 40:1 metal gearbox, with a 6 mm D output shaft, a Hall encoder board at its rear and a six-pin socket. At 12 V it turns 300 rpm unloaded and stalls at 10 kg cm (0.98 N m) and 4 A. Its four M3 holes fit the brackets of Yahboom's aluminium alloy chassis kits; the brackets and couplings come with those kits, not with the motor sold alone.
components.product: L-type 520 Encoder DC Reduction Motor (Separate motor)

components.name: Yahboom battery pack, 7.4 V 2000 mAh

It comes with the Raspbot V2, MicroROS-Pi5, ESP32 MicroROS, Roboduino V2 and MSPM0 smart car kits and is not sold alone.

components.name: 7.4 V 6600 mAh battery for RDK X3 Robot

components.name: 12 V 2200 mAh battery for MicroROS V2
components.description: The battery pack of Yahboom's MicroROS V2 kit: 12 V, 2200 mAh, about 58 x 70 x 19 mm, in a blue sleeve with a white label, a charging socket on one lead and an angled plug for the robot on the other. It comes with the kit and is not sold alone.

components.name: LEGO Mindstorms NXT 8527 Touch Sensor on the Tri-bot's front attachment
components.description: The NXT Touch Sensor on the attachment the Tri-bot's instructions build at its front, which goes on the Tri-bot (lego_8527_tribot_chassis) at its front seat: its button forward, behind a paddle, an axle 6 hung from an angle connector that pivots on a long pin, with a 12-tooth bevel gear on it in front of the button and an axle 7 across its foot; something in the robot's way swings the paddle back, and the gear presses the button. It tells whether its button is pressed. The two claws, which the Tri-bot's third motor opens and closes on axles of their own, are left out, and so are the gears that turn them. The ultrasonic sensor (lego_8527_ultrasonic_sensor) sits on an axle 7 across the attachment's top, at its sonar connector.

components.name: LEGO Mindstorms NXT 8527 Ultrasonic Sensor on the Tri-bot's touch sensor attachment

It measures the distance to the nearest object in front of it with sound.

components.name: Drawing Arm — four-toe channel dock
components.description: Machined aluminium channel bridge, partial foot-locating cups, four removable toe clamps and under-channel backing strips. Includes the modelled fixing hardware. Retains the existing hole-free footed arm base. Metal manufacturing candidate, not a print job.

fabrication.description: Machine a bridge, four toe clamps, four heel spacers and two backing strips in aluminium that clamp the Drawing Arm's base on two Strafer channels, and fit them with M4 screws, washers and nuts.

files.label: Dock bridge
files.note: Milled from 9 mm aluminium plate: 6 mm rails and seats, 3 mm walls for the locating cups

files.label: Toe clamp
files.note: 4 mm aluminium plate, cut or profiled and deburred

files.label: Toe clamp drawing
files.note: No kerf or cutter compensation

files.label: Heel spacer
files.note: Aluminium tube or spacer, 8 mm outside, 4.5 mm inside, 13 mm long

files.label: Backing strip
files.note: 2 mm aluminium sheet

files.label: Backing strip drawing
files.note: No kerf or cutter compensation

buy.item: M4 × 20 socket-cap screw, for the bridge
M4 × 30 socket-cap screw, for the toe clamps
M4 full nut, 7 mm across flats, 3.2 mm high
M4 Form A washer, 4.3 mm inside, 9 mm outside, 0.8 mm thick

steps: Before building, confirm against your manufacturing tolerances the tight fit of the arm's 12 mm feet in the 12.6 mm cups, 0.3 mm all round, and the 0.511 mm gap between a foot and the nearest washer.
Mill the dock bridge from 9 mm aluminium plate; its stepped locating cups need milling, a single flat laser cut cannot make them.
Cut or profile the four toe clamps from 4 mm aluminium plate and deburr them.
Make the four heel spacers from aluminium tube, 8 mm outside, 4.5 mm inside and 13 mm long.
Cut the two backing strips from 2 mm aluminium sheet.
The drawings carry no kerf or cutter compensation; add your own.
Place the two backing strips inside the two Strafer channels.

Before the arm goes on, bolt the bridge down through its four holes with the M4 × 20 screws: a washer on top, the bridge, the channel wall, the backing strip, a washer and a nut below; the rear bolt heads end up under the edge of the arm's base.
Set the Drawing Arm's four feet into the four locating cups; the arm, its servos and its screws are in the arm's own list.

Fit the four heel spacers and the four toe clamps with the M4 × 30 screws: a washer on top, the clamp, the heel spacer, the bridge, a washer and a nut below; the toes press on the top face of the arm's base plate.
Use a 3 mm hex driver for the screw heads and a 7 mm wrench for the nuts; the clamp screw heads stay reachable with the arm in place.
Keep the yaw servo's connector window underneath and the open centre of the bridge clear.
Check the screw tips: nominally 4.7 mm beyond the nut for the bridge screws and 2.2 mm for the clamp screws.
limits: The arm's base has no mounting holes; the dock holds it only by the cups, which locate the feet sideways, and the toe clamps, which stop it lifting.
Do not infer a tightening torque from the CAD; the compression of the printed base and the clamp preload need a physical test.
Clamp preload, loads, strength, physical fit, the arm's swept motion and operation are not confirmed.
Thread engagement and material contact pressure are not simulated.
6061-T6 aluminium is proposed for the bridge and the clamps; no strength calculation was made.
Do not print the dock's pieces; they are machined in metal.
The dock assumes the measured 2.5 mm channel wall.
The dock routes no cables and adds no electrics.

components.name: Drawing Arm — detailed STS3215, ribbed links, parked
components.description: Four original STS3215 joints in the existing parked pose, detailed source servo geometry, ribbed polymer links and original captured footed base. Joint frames and link masses are declared; physical fit, motion clearance, load capacity and hardware control remain unqualified.

fabrication.description: Reference print files and partial hardware selection for the Drawing Arm with four Feetech STS3215 servos. Rear-servo fastener selection must be completed before fabrication.

files.label: Base plate
files.note: Solid PLA

files.label: Shoulder bracket
files.note: Solid PLA; check bridging or supports for its horizontal round bores

files.label: Ribbed shoulder link
files.note: Solid PLA; 4 mm web with outer ribs adding 3 mm

files.label: Ribbed elbow link
files.note: Solid PLA; 4 mm web with outer ribs adding 3 mm

files.label: Pen holder
files.note: Solid PLA; check bridging or supports for its horizontal round bores

buy.item: Feetech STS3215 servo, 12 V (ST-3215-C018)
Rear-servo self-tapping fastener selection unresolved; 16 positions require qualification before fabrication
BOSSARD BN 3 article 1003755, ISO 4762 M3 × 6 fully threaded steel socket-cap screw
BOSSARD BN 3 article 1003798, ISO 4762 M3 × 12 fully threaded steel socket-cap screw
Pen, 6.6–10 mm in diameter

steps: Print each piece in solid PLA as it lies in its file; each is already laid on its print face.
In the slicer, check bridging or supports for the horizontal round bores of the shoulder bracket and the pen holder; the ribbed links have no overhang below 45°.

Do not fabricate the rear-servo fastening from the original screw markers. Their old nominal 8 mm base screws and 6 mm rear screws exceed the retained blind pilot depths. The manufacturer's supplied 2 × 6 mm self-tapping screws lack the point and thread dimensions needed to qualify these stacks.

The ribbed links retain their four M3 horn holes. The modeled M3 × 6 screws pass through 4 mm printed pads into the nominal 2.5 mm horn thickness; actual thread fit and retention still require checking.

Put the pen in the pen holder. The modeled M3 × 12 clamp is backed out 0.3 mm from its former position so its nominal flat tip contacts the modeled 10 mm pen without penetrating it; adjust for the actual pen and do not infer a tightening torque.
Set the arm's base in its separate dock, which clamps it by its four feet; the dock's screws, washers and nuts are in the dock's own list.
limits: The arm is meant to stand still in its parked pose (yaw 0, shoulder 1.10, elbow 2.20 and wrist −2.00 rad): the servos' holding power, moving into this pose and holding it under vibration are not confirmed, and the pose is no transport lock.
The drawing, strength and simulation results of the original table-mounted Drawing Arm do not carry over to this version.
Physical fit, motion clearance, load capacity, wiring and control are not confirmed.

Sixteen rear-servo fasteners remain head-only placeholders, not fabrication-ready hardware. Their purchase identity, head and point dimensions, effective thread engagement and retention remain unresolved; the old nominal M2 lengths are not assembly instructions.
Seventeen M3 screws now include their complete dimensional shanks and hex sockets. Helical threads, production tolerances, horn thread fit, clamping force and preload are not modeled or qualified.
The stiffness of the ribbed links, cable flex, heat, fatigue and vibration are not checked.
The 12 V supply, the servo bus adapter, the current draw, the servo IDs and the controls are not specified; the arm adds no electronics or harness.
Do not mix the original links with a different servo geometry variant.
No printer settings are given beyond solid PLA.
Thread engagement and material contact pressure are not simulated.
The room for the pen was modelled for a pen 10 mm across and 140 mm long.

components.name: L2 — removable four-screw sensor cap
components.description: Small annular cap with four vendor-aligned L2 holes and three externally accessible service screws. Four M3x8 sensor screws insert 3.5 mm after the 4 mm cap and 0.5 mm washers. PETG prototype candidate.

fabrication.description: Print one flat PETG cap that carries the Unitree L2 lidar on its fork at the front of the Strafer, or on the ROSOrin's low roof adapter, and fit it with M3 screws and washers.

files.label: Sensor cap
files.note: PETG by FDM, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layers; flat, underside on the bed

buy.item: ISO 4762 M3 × 8 socket head screw, for the L2
ISO 4762 M3 × 12 socket head screw, for the three service screws
ISO 7089 M3 washer, 7 mm outside, 3.2 mm inside, 0.5 mm thick

steps: Print the sensor cap in PETG by FDM with a 0.4 mm nozzle and 0.2 mm layers, flat with its underside on the bed.
Fit the fork to the Strafer first (or the roof adapter to the ROSOrin); the fork's or the adapter's own list has the three M3 nuts that hold this cap, and the fork's its M4 screws, washers and nuts.
With the cap off the robot, fasten the L2 to the cap from underneath with the four M3 × 8 screws, each with a 0.5 mm washer.
Lower the cap onto the crown of the fork (or onto the adapter) so the four L2 screw heads go into its reliefs.
Fit the three M3 × 12 service screws with washers from outside into the nuts held in the fork.
Route the L2 cable rearward through the open rear and underside of the fork; do not use the sensor housing as a support.
To service the L2, remove the cap and the L2 together by the three service screws.
limits: No print has been made; physical fit, strength, vibration and load are not tested.
PETG with a 0.4 mm nozzle and 0.2 mm layers is an assumed process, not a tested strength specification.
The M3 × 8 screws go 3.5 mm into the L2; the L2 manual allows at most 6 mm.
The four L2 holes follow the L2's own uneven hole pattern; do not replace them with a square pattern.
No tightening torque is given; follow the fastener and sensor suppliers' instructions. The clamp load on the printed cap is not tested.
Cable selection and bend radius are not checked.

A tall Drawing Arm behind the scanner blocks some directions, so the mount alone gives no clear 360° view; load capacity, driving stability, sensor calibration, water resistance and wiring are not established either.
The Unitree L2 is bought separately; it is not part of this cap.

fabrication.description: Machine one aluminium arm plate and two backing strips that hold a ROBOTIS OpenManipulator-X arm 10 mm above the roof of the ROSbot XL, and fit them with M4 screws, washers and nuts.

files.label: Arm plate
files.note: 84 × 104 mm, from 10 mm aluminium stock

files.label: Arm plate drawing
files.note: Outline and drill layer; the layers named REFERENCE are counterbores to machine, not through cuts

files.label: Backing strip
files.note: 2 mm aluminium, 76 × 16 mm, holes Ø4.5

buy.item: M4 × 16 socket head cap screw, ISO 4762
M4 Form A washer, 9 mm outside, 4.3 mm inside, 0.8 mm thick
M4 hex nut, ISO 4032

steps: Machine the arm plate from 10 mm aluminium stock; 6061-T6 is a proposed stock, not a strength claim.
Profile the plate first, then drill it and machine the counterbores on the opposite side; the internal corners of the outline are R3.
Work from the STEP, which defines the counterbores; the drawing's REFERENCE layers are machining instructions, not laser cuts.
Deburr all edges without changing the seating faces or the hole positions.
Cut the two backing strips from 2 mm aluminium and drill them to Ø4.5; they are short so that their ends miss the supports under the roof.
Reuse the arm's four original M2.5 × 20 screws and four X-SP spacer rings, or buy the compatible ROBOTIS mounting hardware.

Off the robot, fit the four spacer rings to the arm's case and fasten it to the plate with the four M2.5 × 20 screws from below, through the counterbores; they cannot be reached once the plate is mounted.
Open or remove the cover of the ROSbot XL as its service procedure allows.
Offer the two backing strips from below the roof, keeping room for a tool to reach the four nuts.

Seat the arm and plate over the four roof holes and fit the four M4 × 16 screws, a washer on top in the plate's counterbore, and a washer and a nut below; a driver reaches the heads from above beside the arm's case.

Before closing the chassis, check the room for wiring and electronics, that the nuts stay in place, the screw protrusion (nominal 1.2 mm beyond the nut) and a tightening torque suited to the real materials.
Route the arm cable into the space left for service, with strain relief.
limits: Do not substitute longer screws for the arm's M2.5 × 20 screws.
To service the arm's screws under the plate, remove the four M4 screws first; do not try to tighten the buried M2.5 heads through the robot.
Do not print these pieces; they are structural metal parts.
The maker's CAD of the ROSbot XL has no internal electronics: check on the real robot that the strips and nuts under the roof clear the inside and can be reached.
The stack is drawn for the 3 mm top plate of the ROSbot XL, as its manual gives it.
The depth of thread engagement in the arm's case is not certified.

A conservative bound puts the arm (0.7 kg) and a 0.5 kg payload, 1.2 kg in all, at 392 mm: 4.615 N·m, or 76.9 N across the 60 mm fore-aft bolt span, before prying, braking or dynamic loads; these are load demands, not allowable loads.
Roof bending, screw preload, fatigue, tipping of the robot and use while driving are not confirmed; no FEA or physical test was made.
The motion of the arm cable is not modelled.

fabrication.description: Print one tray and one removable guard that hold a Raspberry Pi 5 at the rear of the Hiwonder Ackermann chassis, and fit them with metal spacers, screws and M4 bolts.

buy.item: M2.5 female/female spacer for the Raspberry Pi, 8 mm long, 5 mm across flats, steel
M3 female/female spacer for the guard, 25 mm long, 5.5 mm across flats, steel
M2.5 × 6 countersunk screw, 90°, head 5 mm across and 1.5 mm high, for the Raspberry Pi spacers
M3 × 8 countersunk screw, DIN 7991, head 6 mm across and 1.7 mm high, for the guard spacers
buy.note: Confirm the head size with your supplier

buy.item: M2.5 × 5 socket screw with a 0.5 mm washer, 5 mm outside, for the Raspberry Pi
M3 × 6 socket screw with a 0.5 mm washer, 7 mm outside, for the guard
Spacer, 8 mm outside, 4.3 mm inside, 4 mm long, nickel-plated brass (Wurth Elektronik 963040174)
M4 × 16 bolt with two 0.8 mm washers and an M4 nut

steps: Print the Pi carrier tray and the removable guard separately.
Off the robot, fasten the four 8 mm Raspberry Pi spacers to the tray with the M2.5 × 6 countersunk screws from below.
In the same way, fasten the four 25 mm guard spacers to the tray with the M3 × 8 countersunk screws from below.

Seat the tray on the four-hole plate pattern at the rear of the Hiwonder Ackermann chassis, with a 4 mm brass spacer between the tray and the plate at each hole; the spacers lift the tray clear of two chassis screw heads.
Fasten it with the four M4 × 16 bolts, a 0.8 mm washer above the tray and one under the plate, and an M4 nut from below.
Fit the Raspberry Pi 5 on its four holes with the M2.5 × 5 screws and 0.5 mm washers.

Route the connectors and ribbons before fitting the guard: the header ribbon leaves through the GPIO opening, the USB, Ethernet, USB-C and HDMI ports stay open, and the SD card comes out at the short edge.
Fit the removable guard on its spacers with the four M3 × 6 screws and 0.5 mm washers.
limits: Physical fit is not confirmed; the CAD fit check is no load rating.
Strength, vibration and electrical behaviour are not confirmed.
No print material or print settings are specified.
The hardware sizes are nominal; no tightening torque or supplier tolerance is given.
All threads are metal; no screw threads into the printed pieces.
The chassis nuts go on from below, so you need access under the plate.
Remove the guard before servicing the board screws or the ribbon latches; some chassis bolts can only be reached with the Raspberry Pi removed.
Room for the Raspberry Pi Active Cooler was checked only against a reference outline: cooling, cable plug bodies and the cooler's push pins must be checked on the real parts.
The Raspberry Pi 5 is bought separately; the carrier adds no power regulation, motor controllers, wiring or drivers.

Place the existing 4 mm printed seat against the front-right channel wall at the original four-hole pattern. The source channel wall is 2.5 mm thick.

At each host axis place one 1 mm washer outside the print, pass an M4×16 screw inward, then install one 1 mm washer and the complete locking nut inside the channel. Face the nut collar away from the wall.

Cable routing, cable bend radius, full sensing performance and installed physical camera retention remain unqualified.

Deburr the edges.
Check the fit of the arm's feet in the frame against the actual printed arm.

Reach the inside of the chassis as the actual robot allows, without assuming that the roof comes off.
Tell the backing strips apart: the outer one has a 9 mm rounded profile with a trimmed nose edge, the inner one is 12 mm wide.
Raise each backing strip flat and vertically through the open underside of the chassis, lined up with its holes; the outer one goes under the forward row, its trimmed nose edge forward.

Insert the M3 × 30 screws with their washers; each toe clamp overlaps the base plate and bears on a heel spacer.

Two108 mm backing strips give2 mm nominal end-block clearance at Y±64 mm sites; unchanged OEM plate/fastener stack. Physical fit, loads and moving workspaces remain unqualified.

fabrication.description: Machine one aluminium arm plate and two 108 mm backing strips that hold one arm of an opposing OpenManipulator-X pair on the Strafer's channels, and fit them with M4 screws, washers and nuts.

files.label: Arm plate
files.note: 160 × 112 × 10 mm aluminium; 6061-T6 is a proposed stock, not a load rating

files.label: Arm plate drawing
files.note: The counterbore layers are machining references, not through cuts

files.label: 108 mm backing strip
files.note: 108 × 10 × 2 mm aluminium, Ø4.5 holes at 88 mm pitch

buy.item: M4 × 16 socket screw, ISO 4762
M4 Form A washer, 9 × 4.3 × 0.8 mm
M4 nut, ISO 4032

steps: Make two of these mounts for the pair of arms: on the left one the arm faces forward, on the right one it faces rearward, on the same 40 × 22 mm pattern turned 180 degrees.
Machine the arm plate from aluminium; the STEP defines its outline, the Ø4.5 chassis holes with their recessed Ø9.6 counterbores, and the arm's Ø2.7/Ø6 counterbores underneath.
Machine or cut the two backing strips from aluminium, with Ø4.5 holes at 88 mm pitch.
Use the STEP files as the geometry to make; the counterbore layers of the drawings are references, not through cuts.
Deburr without changing the seating faces or the hole positions.
Reuse the arm's four original M2.5 × 20 screws and four X-SP spacer rings, or get the compatible ROBOTIS mounting hardware.
Off the robot, fit the spacer rings and the four M2.5 × 20 screws from the underside of the plate, keeping the arm maker's screw and spacer stack.
Before assembly, check your tools, the wiring and the access from below: from the top a driver within 8 mm across, from below a socket or extension at most 10 mm outside diameter.
Offer the backing strips vertically from below the open channels; they end 2 mm short of the quad blocks.
Seat the arm and plate on top of the Strafer's front and central channels, over existing Ø4 holes; no new holes are needed.
Fit the four M4 × 16 screws with a washer on top and one below, and the nuts.
Recheck the screw protrusion, that the nuts stay in place, and a preload suited to the real parts.
limits: Do not substitute longer screws for the arm's M2.5 × 20 screws.
To service the arm's screws under the plate, remove the four M4 screws; do not try to reach them through the installed robot.
Do not print these pieces as structural substitutes; they are metal parts.
Do not use 112 mm backing strips here: at these positions they touch the chassis end blocks.
The tool sizes leave 0.5 mm nominal clearance at the sides; they are room for tools, not a guarantee that a bought tool fits.

M4 shaft and chassis hole tolerances, the 2 mm end clearance, clamp preload, bending of the plate and channels, fatigue, payload limits, tipping and use while driving are not confirmed; no FEA or physical test was made.
Thread engagement is not certified.
The two arms were only checked standing still: collisions while moving, both working at once and cable sweep are not confirmed.
The pair is a fixed mechanical arrangement, not an electrically integrated robot.

components.name: 5V, 11A Step-Down Voltage Regulator D42V110F5
components.description: Pololu D42V110F5 step-down regulator, a bare board with a regulated 5 V output nominal and four M2 mounting holes. Wires, terminal blocks and headers are sold separately; the board does not negotiate USB Power Delivery.

components.name: 5203 Series Yellow Jacket Planetary Gear Motor (19.2:1 Ratio, 24mm Length 8mm REX® Shaft, 312 RPM, 3.3 - 5V Encoder)

Its 19.2:1 gearbox gives 312 rpm unloaded at 12 V; the output is an 8 mm REX shaft. The magnetic quadrature encoder and its separate 3.3–5 V supply are not represented by this Motor profile.

components.name: goBILDA 1209-0001-0001 mount for 12 V NiMH nested battery

The flexible strap is supplied and required but omitted because its dimensions are not published.

components.name: Strafer Pi 5 and dual Motoron open carrier
components.description: Authored open Strafer Pi 5 carrier with two Motoron boards retained by eight 11 mm M2.5 metal standoffs, four 2 mm nylon spacers and four top screws. Guard removed; prototype pending physical fit.

fabrication.description: Print one PETG carrier tray and stack a Raspberry Pi 5 and two Motoron boards on it with metal standoffs, nylon spacers and screws; four M4 screws hold it on the Strafer.

files.label: Carrier tray
files.note: PETG, FDM, 1:1 scale in millimetres, flat underside on the build plate

files.label: Carrier tray, editable CAD
files.note: The same single printed body; print only one tray

buy.item: M2.5 female/female steel standoff, 8 mm body, 5 mm across flats (Wurth 970080151)
M2.5×6 countersunk screw, 5 mm head diameter, 1.5 mm head height (Aspen ME300-25045X6)
M2.5 washer, OD 5 mm, ID 2.7 mm, thickness 0.5 mm
Pololu 1952 aluminum M2.5 male/female standoff, 11 mm body, 4 mm across flats, 6 mm male thread
buy.note: Two Motoron 5054 controllers include these eight in total

buy.item: Pololu 1970 nylon spacer, length 2 mm, OD 4 mm, ID 2.7 mm
M2.5×6 socket-head screw, Ø4.5 mm head, 2.5 mm head height, 2 mm hex drive (Aspen ME266-25045X6)
buy.note: The M2.5×6 Phillips screws supplied with the controllers are an alternative

buy.item: M4×12 screw
M4 washer, OD 9 mm, ID 4.2 mm, thickness 0.8 mm
M4 nut, 7 mm across flats, height 3.2 mm

steps: Print one tray in PETG at 1:1 scale with its flat underside on the build plate.
Check the fit of the holes and countersinks before assembly.
Before stacking, enable I²C1 on the Pi and set the second Motoron to address 0x11; leave the first at 0x10.
Attach the four 8 mm female/female standoffs to the tray with the countersunk screws from below; their heads recess beneath the tray's underside.

Bolt the tray to the Strafer's rear-left computer-carrier holes with the four M4×12 screws, one M4 washer above and one below each chassis joint, then the M4 nut. The nuts need access from underneath.
Seat the Pi on the four 8 mm standoffs, place one 0.5 mm M2.5 washer above each hole of its board, then screw in four of the 11 mm male/female standoffs.
Fit the first Motoron onto those four standoffs and the Pi's 40-pin header.
Place one 2 mm nylon spacer over each mounting hole of the first Motoron, then screw the other four 11 mm standoffs in through the spacers and the board.
Fit the second Motoron onto the four upper standoffs and the first Motoron's header, and secure it with the four M2.5×6 socket-head screws.
Inspect the clearance of the terminal-block leads and solder fillets; follow Pololu's stacking instructions for the Motoron and trim the leads where necessary before applying power.
limits: PETG is the prototype material; print settings, tolerances and load capacity have not been established.
All dimensions are nominal; physical fit, retention torque, vibration, temperature and lead clearance must be checked on the real stack.
All threads are in separate metal hardware; nothing screws into the print.
Do not leave out the 0.5 mm washers on the Pi: they leave a nominal 0.43 mm gap between the Pi's header and the first Motoron's socket.
The terminal-block leads clear the lower terminal blocks by approximately 0.55 mm on nominal dimensions; real lead length and solder fillets need inspection.
This is an open stack; do not add a guard or guard standoffs to it.
The Pi carries no Active Cooler in this stack, and its cooling was not checked.

components.name: Strafer D42V110F5 carrier
components.description: Authored, printable Strafer front-left carrier for the Pololu D42V110F5, with four captive M2 nuts, full through screws and four M4 chassis bolts. Prototype pending physical/thermal qualification.

fabrication.description: Print one PETG carrier for the Pololu D42V110F5 regulator and bolt it to the Strafer's front-left side rail; four M2 screws in captive nuts hold the regulator.

files.label: Regulator carrier
files.note: PETG, FDM, 1:1 scale in millimetres, flat underside on the build plate, support bosses facing up

files.label: Regulator carrier, editable CAD
files.note: The same single printed body; print one carrier, not one of each file

buy.item: M2 × 14 socket screw, DIN 912 (Accu SSCF-M2-14-A2)
M2 nut, DIN 934, 4 mm across flats, 1.6 mm high (Accu HPN-M2-A2)
M4 × 12 socket screw, DIN 912 (Accu SSCF-M4-12-A2)
M4 washer, OD 9, ID 4.3, thickness 0.9 mm (Accu HPW-M4-A2)
M4 nut, DIN 934, 7 mm across flats, 3.2 mm high (Accu HPN-M4-A2)

steps: Print one carrier in PETG at 1:1 scale, with its flat underside on the build plate and the support bosses facing up.
Check the Ø2.4 and Ø4.6 holes and the nut pockets of the print before fitting any hardware.
Off the robot, insert an M2 nut into the pocket under each of the four bosses.
Still off the robot, set the regulator on the four bosses and fasten it from above with the four M2 × 14 screws.
Fit the carrier before the front-left motor, or take that motor out first: the M4 nuts need access inside the rail.

Bolt the carrier to the four Ø4 holes in the top of the Strafer's front-left side rail with the four M4 × 12 screws: one washer under each screw head, then one washer and the nut under the rail's 2.5 mm top wall.
limits: PETG is the prototype material; print settings, tolerances and load capacity have not been established.
All dimensions are nominal; printed tolerances, tightening torque, heat, vibration, electrical insulation and load are not confirmed.
There are no printed threads; the pockets only keep the M2 nuts from turning.
By the nominal dimensions the M2 × 14 screws pass through the full nut and end above the rail, and the M4 × 12 screws stand 0.5 mm past their nuts.
The regulator and its wiring are separate and are not part of this carrier.

components.name: Strafer U2D2 Power Hub service carrier
components.description: Authored vented carrier retaining a ROBOTIS U2D2 Power Hub on the Strafer front-right side rail with four M4 bolts and four separately purchased M3 steel standoffs. Fabrication option; physical fit and loads remain unqualified.

fabrication.description: Print one vented PETG carrier, fit the ROBOTIS U2D2 Power Hub on it with four M3 steel spacers and bolt it to the Strafer's front-right side rail with four M4 screws.

files.label: Power Hub carrier
files.note: PETG, flat side down on the build plate; millimetres, nominal 3 mm floor

files.label: Power Hub carrier, editable CAD
files.note: The same single plastic body

buy.item: M3 steel female/female spacer, through thread, length 10 mm, 5.5 mm across flats (Würth 970100321)
M3 countersunk socket screw, ISO 10642, overall length 8 mm, 90-degree head (Accu SSK-M3-8-A4)
M3 × 6 mm cap head screw (Accu SSCF-M3-6-A2)
M3 washer, OD 7 mm, ID 3.2 mm, thickness 0.55 mm (Accu HPW-M3-A2)
M4 × 12 mm cap head screw (Accu SSCF-M4-12-A2)
M4 washer, OD 9 mm, ID 4.3 mm, thickness 0.9 mm (Accu HPW-M4-A2)
M4 nut, 7 mm across flats, 3.2 mm high (Accu HPN-M4-A2)

steps: Print one carrier in PETG with its flat side down.
Finish and inspect the printed bores and countersinks before assembly.
Off the robot, fasten the four M3 spacers to the carrier with the four countersunk screws from the underside.
Bolt the carrier to the four holes of the Strafer's front-right side rail with the four M4 × 12 screws: one washer under each screw head, then one washer and the nut under the rail's 2.5 mm wall.
Set the Power Hub on the four spacers, put an M3 washer on each hole and fasten it with the four M3 × 6 screws.
Leave off the plastic feet and nuts supplied with the Power Hub; they are not used here.
limits: Physical fit, print strength, preload, vibration, temperature and load ratings are not established; print settings have not been tested.
The screw stacks are nominal calculations; thread tolerance and preload are not confirmed.

By those calculations the 10 mm spacers leave about 6.93 mm between the lowest feature under the Power Hub and the carrier floor, the two M3 screws in each spacer end 1.15 mm apart, and the M4 screws stand 1.5 mm past their nuts.
The Power Hub, the U2D2 and their cables are separate purchases.

components.name: ROBOTIS U2D2 USB-C communication interface
components.description: ROBOTIS U2D2 Type-C USB communication converter with one TTL DYNAMIXEL, one RS-485 DYNAMIXEL and one UART connector. components.name: ROBOTIS U2D2 Power Hub board
components.description: ROBOTIS U2D2 Power Hub board with its four stock U2D2 retaining rivets, a switched shared external-power rail, three TTL and three RS-485 sockets, barrel/Molex/terminal inputs and the manufacturer's four-rivet seat for the separately sold U2D2. The official board CAD omits the supplied supports, nuts, rivets and cables. The four required stock rivets are installed for the declared capture; their exact geometry and load rating remain unpublished.

components.name: LiTech Power LRL1220 12.8 V 20 Ah LiFePO4 battery
components.description: LRL1220 LiFePO4 battery with an internal BMS, 12.8 V nominal, 20 Ah nominal capacity, a published 10-14.6 V operating range, 20 A maximum continuous discharge and 30 A discharge for 1-3 seconds. The manufacturer lists it on backorder with a quotation request; no purchase price is known.

components.name: Strafer lower LRL1220 cradle
components.description: Authored lower Strafer cradle for the LiTech LRL1220. A CNC aluminium floor, four 45.5 mm spacer columns, four M4x60 through bolts, two genuine goBILDA cinch plates and a 600 mm Panduit TTR-20R0 strip retain the pack. Prototype with nominal CAD fit; structural loads, manufacturing tolerances and physical fit remain unqualified.

fabrication.description: Machine one aluminium battery cradle and four spacer columns for the LiTech LRL1220, and fit them under the Strafer's rear bay with M4 screws, two goBILDA cinch plates and a Panduit strip.

files.label: Battery cradle
files.note: 6061 aluminium; 4 mm floor, 8 mm high retaining rim, 184 x 80 mm inside pocket, 216 x 360 x 12 mm overall; millimetres

files.label: Spacer column
files.note: Aluminium; 8 mm outside diameter, 4.5 mm through bore, 45.5 mm length; millimetres

buy.item: M4 x 60 mm cap screw, ISO 4762
M4 x 16 mm cap screw, ISO 4762
M4 x 0.7 nylock nut, 7 mm across flats, 4.85 mm high
buy.note: Four more come with the cinch kit; the cradle uses 8 in all

buy.item: goBILDA 1209-0032-0001 cinch kit
buy.note: Its two rigid plates and four nuts are used; its 250 mm strip and its M4 x 12 mm screws are not

buy.item: Panduit TTR-20R0 strip, 19.1 mm wide, 0.9 mm thick, cut to 600 mm

steps: Machine the cradle from 6061 aluminium with its clearance holes and both through-slots as drawn.
Keep the central support under the two cinch plates, and keep the closed retaining rim and its clearance to the battery when choosing how to finish the corners.
Turn and drill the four spacer columns from aluminium stock, or cut them from tube of 8 mm outside diameter and 4.5 mm bore.
Face both ends of each column to the 45.5 mm length and deburr the bore. No taps are needed.
Cut 600 mm of the Panduit strip.
Place the cradle below the Strafer's rear bay.

Put the four spacer columns between the cradle floor and the underside of the chassis's top web, at the four existing holes of the web. The channels open downward; there is no bottom web to drill or clamp to.
Insert the four M4 x 60 mm screws from above through the 2.5 mm web, the columns and the 4 mm floor, and fit four nylock nuts underneath.
Fasten both cinch plates on the central support by their outer 32 mm hole pairs with the four M4 x 16 mm screws and the four remaining nuts.
Point the strap slots of the plates toward the battery pocket and line each slot up with the opening in the floor.
Thread the 600 mm strip through the two slots and underneath the floor.
Seat the battery inside the retaining rim.
Wrap the strip over the battery and close it with at least 50 mm of overlap.
Keep the battery terminals exposed and route the electrical cables separately.
limits: These are nominal prototype drawings; manufacturing tolerances, physical fit and structural loads are not confirmed.
Tightening torque is not specified; the nominal thread protrusion past the nuts under the cradle floor is 3.15 mm.
Do not use the cinch kit's M4 x 12 mm screws on the plates: they are too short for the 8 mm stack of plate and floor.
The strip must keep at least 50 mm of overlap; its path leaves 76.79 mm on a battery 162 mm high and 62.79 mm at the battery's 169 mm maximum height.
The loop strength of the strip is not a load rating for the whole cradle.
The longest screws end 16 mm above level ground with the 104 mm wheels.
Ground travel, vibration, arm movement, strap wear, cable clearance and dynamic loads have not been tested.
Fatigue, shock, floor stiffness, bolt preload and access to the battery terminals while an arm moves are not confirmed either.

components.name: Printable BLF-1215A tray on the Strafer rear-right rail
components.description: Printable BLF-1215A tray on the Strafer rear-right rail. Authored printable tray, 4 aluminium spacer tubes, M4 hardware and two real Panduit straps. Nominal prototype geometry; print strength, tolerances and loads remain unqualified.

fabrication.description: Print one tray for the Bioenno BLF-1215A battery and cut four aluminium spacer tubes, then fit them to the Strafer's rear-right rail with M4 screws, washers, lock nuts and two hook-and-loop strips.

files.label: Battery tray
files.note: One solid, flat floor down; millimetres

files.label: Battery tray, exact solid
files.note: The same single tray, an alternative to the print file; millimetres

files.label: Spacer tube
files.note: Aluminium tube, cut or turned: OD 8, bore 4.5, length 32 mm

buy.item: goBILDA 2800-0004-0045 M4 × 45 screw, zinc-plated, 7 mm head diameter, 4 mm head height
goBILDA 2801-0004-0008 washer, zinc-plated steel, OD 8 × ID 4 × 1 mm
goBILDA 2812-0004-0007 M4 lock nut with nylon insert, 7 mm across flats
Panduit TTR-20R0 hook-and-loop strip, 19.1 × 0.9 mm, cut to 470 mm
buy.note: Comes as a 6.1 m roll

steps: Print the battery tray as one solid with its flat floor down. Keep all four through holes, the screw-head recesses, the four strap slots and the continuous rim.
Cut or turn the 4 spacer tubes from aluminium: OD 8, bore 4.5, length 32 mm. Their bores are clearance holes; nothing is threaded.
Cut two 470 mm lengths of the hook-and-loop strip.
Put a washer under the head of each M4 × 45 screw and drop the four screws into the counterbores in the tray floor, so that the heads sit below the surface the battery rests on.
Pass each screw through a spacer tube and through the 2.5 mm wall of the Strafer's rear-right rail, and fit a lock nut below it, flat face against the rail and nylon collar down.
Tighten the four screws before the battery goes in.
Thread each strip through its pair of slots in the tray and below the floor.
Set the battery in the tray with its 137 × 78 mm face up.
Wrap each strip over the side stops and the battery and press its ends together with at least 50 mm of overlap.
Keep the place where the battery leads come out free, and route the leads separately.
limits: No print settings, strength or payload rating have been demonstrated; PETG was assumed only to estimate the mass.
Slicing, shrinkage, wear, heat, creep under compression and how firmly the battery is held must be checked on your own print.
The battery has 0.5 mm of clearance on each side and can move up to 1 mm; it is not a friction fit.
Tightening torque is not specified, and the nominal dimensions give no tolerance, preload or load rating.
The thread stands 0.95 mm past the lock nut by the nominal dimensions; thread clearance, insertion torque and locking force of the nut are not established.
Do not leave out the spacer tubes: they provide wheel clearance.
The path of the strips is drawn only; how firmly they hold and whether cables clear them is not established.
Clearance to other payloads, arms and cables on the robot was not checked.

components.name: RobotDSL Gripper
components.description: The RobotDSL Gripper, of the RobotDSL Team's own design: a gripper on one Feetech STS3215 (12 V, ST-3215-C018) servo, its palm screwed onto the horn of a servo of the same kind turning about its length (an arm's wrist roll), its moving finger closing on a fixed one, fingers 55 mm long, every piece printed without supports. Held in one pose: its moving finger upright beside the fixed one, at its joint's zero.

steps: Print each piece in PLA, solid, laid as its file lies; none wants supports.
Set the Feetech STS3215 (12 V, ST-3215-C018)'s zero, its horn fitted as it comes.
Screw the servo to the palm's wall by the rails of its back with four M2 screws, which thread themselves into the rails' pilot holes.

The printed pieces' strength under load was not checked.
The servo's supply, bus adapter and controller are not part of it, and its current was not checked.

steps: Print each piece separately with at least five perimeters and solid screw pads; 0.2 mm layers are a starting process, not a strength qualification.
Inspect and clear all holes and nut windows. Fit four M3 nuts through the cheeks' outside service windows.
Fasten the cheeks to the four existing middle-channel holes with M4 × 14 screws, a washer above and below each joint, and accessible underside nuts.
Off the robot, insert the four M3 × 8 screws and washers from beneath the cap into the L2, checking the 3 mm nominal engagement.
Put the two 2 mm nylon spacers over the MinIMU hole on the separate shelf, then seat the board above them with its header edge facing the open side.

Fasten the IMU with the M2 × 14 screw and top washer through its single original hole, both spacers, and the cap; fit the lower washer and nut beneath the cap. Check that both printed stops clear the board.
Install the populated cap on the cheeks with four M3 × 10 screws and washers. Keep wires below the LiDAR scan plane.
limits: Physical fit, stiffness, vibration, tolerances, clamp preload and full robot operation remain untested.
The IMU side stops have 0.35 mm nominal clearance; printing error can reduce it, so inspect before installation.
Do not combine this portal with an arm bridge using the same middle-channel holes.
Host holes are nominally 4 mm; nominal geometry does not guarantee clearance for an actual M4 screw.
Confirm access to underside nuts and actual cable overmoulds on the built chassis.

goBILDA 2812-0004-0007 M4 lock nut

steps: Print the single tray flat on its floor; preserve all four screw recesses, sidewall access windows, the low lead-side end and side stops and all four strap slots.
Cut or turn four aluminium tubes, OD 8 mm, bore 4.5 mm, length 32 mm.
Fit a washer under each screw head and pass each screw through a tray recess, a tube and the rear-right channel's 2.5 mm web.
Fit each lock nut beneath the channel, flat face upward and nylon collar downward; tighten before placing the battery.
Thread each strip through its two side slots and beneath the tray floor, so the wraps are transverse to the battery long axis.
Seat the pack with its leads above the 6 mm low end stop; wrap both strips around it and engage at least 50 mm of overlap below the tray and around the slot side.

Keep all four metal tubes; their height clears the wheel and keeps the screw tails above the motor.

Battery lead routing is installation work and must not pass beneath the retaining strip.
The drawn overlaps follow the strip underside and outside of the slot; inspect complete engagement after tensioning. No buckle is needed.

Install the additional front caster with its three rollers and retaining clip as described by Pololu.

steps: Print the one-piece carrier with its underside flat; preserve four captive-nut pockets and all six screw bores.
Insert four M2 nuts from underneath, put the PCB on all four bosses and secure it with four M2 × 14 screws.
Place the carrier on the documented two existing top-wall holes; do not combine it with the OMX-left mount on the shared holes.
Place a Ø9 Accu washer under each M4 × 12 screw, pass it through plate and channel, then install a Ø8 goBILDA washer and M4 nut below.
Provide access inside the channels while holding the nuts. Check full nut engagement, PCB support, underside and socket clearance before tightening.
Install the separate board's explicitly selected wiring configuration and provide cable retention; cable hardware and independent servo power distribution are separate operations.
limits: Physical fit, print anisotropy, creep, screw torque, vibration, thermal performance and load capacity are unqualified.
Nominal board-screw projection is 0.40000066 mm; host-screw projection is 0.4 mm. Nominal major thread diameters do not establish fit.
Native CAD establishes bare-board clearance. Actual cable plugs, insertion paths, bend radius, strain relief and nut-driver envelopes remain unqualified.
The fixture mass excludes the separate board, installation wiring and independent arm power distribution.
Do not print the installed assembly STEP; only make/carrier.stl or carrier.step is the fabrication part.

steps: Fit the Pi/guard spacer base screws before the underside boards.
Solder and insulate underside board leads, then attach D42/S13/MinIMU face down with seven M2x14 screws, seven washers and seven nuts.
Fit four chassis bolts over eight 20mm sleeves while Pi is absent; tighten lower M3 nuts from below.
Fit Pi using four M2.5 screws and connect harnesses before fitting guard. Host screw service requires Pi removal.
limits: Physical fit is not confirmed; the CAD fit check is no load rating.
Strength, vibration and electrical behaviour are not confirmed.
No print material or print settings are specified.
The hardware sizes are nominal; no tightening torque or supplier tolerance is given.
All threads are metal; no screw threads into the printed pieces.
The chassis nuts go on from below, so you need access under the deck.
Remove the guard before servicing the board screws or the ribbon latches; some chassis bolts can only be reached with the Raspberry Pi removed.
Room for the Raspberry Pi Active Cooler was checked only against a reference outline: cooling, cable plug bodies and the cooler's push pins must be checked on the real parts.

The two regulators and MinIMU are separate purchased parts. Printed bosses contact their native rear PCB mounting planes; one real MinIMU mounting bolt and a nominal0.2mm lateral-clearance edge cradle retain the IMU.
The 30mm rear shift overhangs the chassis. Nominal static CAD and point contacts do not certify dynamic stability or load capacity.
D42/S13 screw tips project0.4752mm beyond the upper nut nominally; tolerances and PCB crushing/preload require physical qualification.
Pi SD card travels above the new floor webs; connector bodies, wire bend radii and service access require physical confirmation.

steps: Machine the plates from 6.35 mm aluminium. Check the 28.60 mm seats against the actual bearing OD and fit the flanges inboard.
Cut the rounded hex stock to 166.35 mm for the roller and 157 mm for the motor.
Fit the two side plates to the four standoffs. On the roller install two 1/4-inch spacers, the pulley, a 1/4-inch spacer and four wheel–spacer pairs.

Retain both roller ends with a 1/8-inch spacer and a clamp collar. Mount the motor and controller on the sliding plate and secure the pulley between two collars on the output side. Fit the remaining collar at the rear of the motor shaft.
Place the belt over both pulleys. Start at 101.6 mm centre distance, adjust the carriage and tighten its four clamps.

installations.description: Bare-kit sensor layout with four AAA cells retained in the factory battery compartments and a direct series-cell supply. Controller, drive motors and sensor data connections remain unresolved.
limits: The four AAA cells require series wiring across the supplied contacts; preserve the polarity printed on the chassis/board documentation. The maker does not publish a guaranteed cell discharge-voltage range.
A populated control board and drive motors are still absent. These fixtures consume the chassis control-board mounting holes and have not been checked against populated board clearance.
Physical fit, printing, strength, wiring, sensor response and commissioning are not established by this mechanical example.
Retain conservative Core collision findings; different neighbours require a new clearance and sensing review.

installations.title: forward RGB observation
installations.description: A low rounded saddle follows the front mounting pair and keeps the rear compute carrier separate.
limits: The retained six AA cells feed the screwed Romi motor driver and both motors. Their discharge voltage range remains unpublished; the Pi 5 still needs a retained supply capable of at least 3 A at 5 V.
Camera data and nominal 3.3 V power use CAM0 and the Pi 5 camera FFC cable; connector compatibility does not establish the unpublished supply tolerances.
Physical fit, printing, strength, wiring, sensor response and commissioning are not established by this mechanical example.

Battery capture preserves all chassis material. Unsupported wheel, motor and deck cavities have also been withdrawn. The coarse chassis box crosses the cells, motors and wheel envelopes; source-accurate material geometry is needed.
Both native casters retain a clearance failure: Core bounds each spherical caster by a cylinder which crosses real socket material. No fictitious cavity or clearance exemption is declared.

Diff_two_caster chassis(ref = "pololu_romi_chassis_kit")
Mount device1_support(ref = "robotdsl_romi_camera3_nose_cage", on = @core/chassis, at = "v3_front_docking_sensor", by = "under_holes")

    Motor motor_left(ref = "pololu_mini_plastic_gearmotor_120_hp_offset_extended", glue = (0, 0.06269, 0, 0, 1, 0), command = @core/board)
    Motor motor_right(ref = "pololu_mini_plastic_gearmotor_120_hp_offset_extended", glue = (0, -0.06269, 0, 0, -1, 0), command = @core/board)
    Standard wheel_left(ref = "pololu_wheel_70x8mm", glue = (0, 0.0704, 0, 0, 1, 0))
    Standard wheel_right(ref = "pololu_wheel_70x8mm", glue = (0, -0.0704, 0, 0, -1, 0))
    Caster caster(ref = "pololu_romi_ball_caster", glue = (-0.06396984067436, -0.00000973866262, -0.02223, 0, 0, -1))
    Caster caster_front(ref = "pololu_romi_ball_caster", glue = (0.0442, 0, -0.0223, 0, 0, -1))

    Mount device1_support(ref = "robotdsl_romi_camera3_nose_cage", on = @core/chassis, at = "v3_front_docking_sensor", by = "under_holes")

    Camera device1_sensor(ref = "raspberry_pi_camera_module_3", on = @core/device1_support, at = "sensor_holes", by = "camera_pcb_holes", power = @core/computer, output = "cam0_power", data = @core/computer, port = "cam0")

    Attachment computer(ref = "raspberry_pi_5_8gb", on = @core/compute_mount, at = "board_holes", by = "mounting_holes")
}

installations.title: Panoramic mapping, downward inspection and near-field front indication
installations.description: Purpose-specific scanner support; panoramic horizon and cable/tool access need the stated arrangement. A roof-to-nose bracket puts the close-range camera over the front edge rather than looking through the roof. A front-edge acoustic yoke puts the transducer ahead of the adjacent OAK fork, with its rear screw access above the roof and the front-right camera site free.
limits: Factory internal Pi 5 retained; no optional external computer is required.
Physical fit, printing, strength, wiring, sensor response and commissioning are not established by this mechanical example.
Retain conservative Core collision findings; different neighbours require a new clearance and sensing review.
installations.snippet:
Mecanum_four_wheel chassis(ref = "husarion_rosbot_xl_mecanum_chassis")
Mount device1_scanner_mount(ref = "robotdsl_rosbot_s3_compact_crown", on = @core/chassis, at = "sight_lidar_spider", by = "under_holes")
Lidar device1_scanner(ref = "husarion_rplidar_s3", on = @core/device1_scanner_mount, at = "scanner_holes", by = "mounting_holes", power = @core/chassis, output = "user_5v")

scope.core:
// Factory internal Pi 5 retained; no optional external computer is required.
// Mechanical candidate; actual mounting interfaces are declared below.
Robot mount_rosbot_s3_floor_near_field {
    intent "Panoramic mapping, downward inspection and near-field front indication"

    Mecanum_four_wheel chassis(ref = "husarion_rosbot_xl_mecanum_chassis")
    Mecanum wheel_front_left(ref = "husarion_rosbot_xl_mecanum_wheel_front_left", glue = (0.085000000010, 0.1, 0, 0, 1, 0))
    Mecanum wheel_front_right(ref = "husarion_rosbot_xl_mecanum_wheel_front_right", glue = (0.085000000010, -0.1, 0, 0, -1, 0))
    Mecanum wheel_rear_left(ref = "husarion_rosbot_xl_mecanum_wheel_rear_left", glue = (-0.085000000010, 0.1, 0, 0, 1, 0))
    Mecanum wheel_rear_right(ref = "husarion_rosbot_xl_mecanum_wheel_rear_right", glue = (-0.085000000010, -0.1, 0, 0, -1, 0))

    Mount device1_scanner_mount(ref = "robotdsl_rosbot_s3_compact_crown", on = @core/chassis, at = "sight_lidar_spider", by = "under_holes")

    Lidar device1_scanner(ref = "husarion_rplidar_s3", on = @core/device1_scanner_mount, at = "scanner_holes", by = "mounting_holes", power = @core/chassis, output = "user_5v")

    Mount device2_support(ref = "robotdsl_rosbot_d405_inspection_arm", on = @core/chassis, at = "sight_camera_rosbot", by = "under_holes")

    RGBD device2_sensor(ref = "realsense_d405", on = @core/device2_support, at = "sensor_holes", by = "tripod_hole", data = @core/chassis, port = "rear_usb_1", power = @core/chassis, output = "rear_usb_1_power")

    Mount device3_support(ref = "robotdsl_rosbot_mb1010_nose_yoke", on = @core/chassis, at = "v3_front_left_sensor", by = "under_holes")

    Ultrasonic device3_sensor(ref = "maxbotix_mb1010_lv_maxsonar_ez1", on = @core/device3_support, at = "sensor_holes", by = "mounting_holes", power = @core/chassis, output = "ext1_3v3")
}

installations.description: Purpose-specific scanner support; panoramic horizon and cable/tool access need the stated arrangement.
limits: Shown Pi 5 has a real mounting chain; motor control, power regulation and electrical/data connections remain unresolved.
Physical fit, printing, strength, wiring, sensor response and commissioning are not established by this mechanical example.
Retain conservative Core collision findings; different neighbours require a new clearance and sensing review.
installations.snippet:
Mecanum_four_wheel chassis(ref = "gobilda_strafer_chassis_kit_104mm")
Mount device1_scanner_mount(ref = "robotdsl_strafer_rplidar_rear_portal", on = @core/chassis, at = "lidar_middle_channel", by = "under_holes")
Lidar device1_scanner(ref = "husarion_rplidar_a2m12", on = @core/device1_scanner_mount, at = "scanner_holes", by = "mounting_holes", data = @core/computer, port = "uart0")

scope.core:
// Shown Pi 5 has a real mounting chain; motor control, power regulation and electrical/data connections remain unresolved.
// Mechanical candidate; actual mounting interfaces are declared below.
Robot mount_strafer_a2_mapping {
    intent "Raised planar mapping with A2"

    Mecanum_four_wheel chassis(ref = "gobilda_strafer_chassis_kit_104mm")

    // The Strafer kit includes these four motors; retained 1:1 miter gears drive its wheel shafts.
    Motor motor_front_left(ref = "gobilda_yellow_jacket_5203_2402_0019", glue = (0.140, 0.156, 0, 1, 0, 0), command = @core/drive_front, channel = "M1")
    Motor motor_front_right(ref = "gobilda_yellow_jacket_5203_2402_0019", glue = (0.140, -0.156, 0, 1, 0, 0), command = @core/drive_front, channel = "M2")
    Motor motor_rear_left(ref = "gobilda_yellow_jacket_5203_2402_0019", glue = (-0.140, 0.156, 0, -1, 0, 0), command = @core/drive_rear, channel = "M1")
    Motor motor_rear_right(ref = "gobilda_yellow_jacket_5203_2402_0019", glue = (-0.140, -0.156, 0, -1, 0, 0), command = @core/drive_rear, channel = "M2")
    Mecanum wheel_front_left(ref = "gobilda_gripforce_mecanum_104mm_fl_rr", glue = (0.168, 0.207, 0, 0, 1, 0))
    Mecanum wheel_front_right(ref = "gobilda_gripforce_mecanum_104mm_fr_rl", glue = (0.168, -0.207, 0, 0, -1, 0))
    Mecanum wheel_rear_left(ref = "gobilda_gripforce_mecanum_104mm_fr_rl", glue = (-0.168, 0.207, 0, 0, 1, 0))
    Mecanum wheel_rear_right(ref = "gobilda_gripforce_mecanum_104mm_fl_rr", glue = (-0.168, -0.207, 0, 0, -1, 0))

    Mount device1_scanner_mount(ref = "robotdsl_strafer_rplidar_rear_portal", on = @core/chassis, at = "lidar_middle_channel", by = "under_holes")

    // Scanner needs at least 4.9 V; the retained 5 V regulator can fall to 4.85 V.
    // Leave its supply unresolved until a suitable retained power stage is selected.
    Lidar device1_scanner(ref = "husarion_rplidar_a2m12", on = @core/device1_scanner_mount, at = "scanner_holes", by = "mounting_holes", data = @core/computer, port = "uart0")

    Mount compute_mount(ref = "robotdsl_strafer_pi5_motoron_carrier", on = @core/chassis, at = "compute_strafer_pi5", by = "under_holes")
    Attachment computer(ref = "raspberry_pi_5_8gb", on = @core/compute_mount, at = "board_holes", by = "mounting_holes", power = @core/regulator)
    MotorDriver drive_front(ref = "pololu_motoron_m2h18v20_dual_high_power_motor_controller_for_raspberry_pi_connectors_soldered", on = @core/compute_mount, at = "motoron_lower", by = "mounting_holes", power = @core/battery, command = @core/computer, port = "i2c1", address = "0x10")
    MotorDriver drive_rear(ref = "pololu_motoron_m2h18v20_dual_high_power_motor_controller_for_raspberry_pi_connectors_soldered", on = @core/compute_mount, at = "motoron_upper", by = "mounting_holes", power = @core/battery, command = @core/computer, port = "i2c1", address = "0x11")

    Mount regulator_mount(ref = "robotdsl_mount_strafer_d42v110f5", on = @core/chassis, at = "regulator_front_left", by = "under_holes")
    Attachment regulator(ref = "pololu_d42v110f5_5v_regulator", on = @core/regulator_mount, at = "board_holes", by = "mounting_holes", power = @core/battery)
    Mount battery_holder(ref = "robotdsl_strafer_gensace_2200_tray", on = @core/chassis, at = "battery_rear_right", by = "mounting_holes")
    Battery battery(ref = "gensace_gea223s25t3gt_lipo_battery", on = @core/battery_holder, at = "battery")
}
